name: SV-Benchmarks, the verification tasks of the Competition on Software Verification 2025
organizers: Dirk Beyer, LMU Munich, and Jan Strejček, Masaryk University, for the competition; the tasks themselves come from hundreds of contributors
layout: sv-benchmarks/c/<family>/*.c beside one *.yml per task, which names the input files, the property file under sv-benchmarks/c/properties/ and the data model; sv-benchmarks/java/ and the Horn clauses are other tracks
terms: the archive is CC-BY-4.0 as a collection; the tasks carry their own licences, listed in sv-benchmarks/LICENSES/ and declared file by file with SPDX headers, from Apache-2.0 to GPL and several attribution licences
note: the citable artefact of SV-COMP 2025, 1.8 GB compressed and 11.8 GB unpacked over 175 thousand files, which is why this repository keeps the manifest only: tools/fetch_upstream.py downloads it into a local cache and the CNF encodings are produced on demand. Member checksums are not recorded here, as for smtqfbv: the list would be longer than the repository. The zip holds the version the competition ran, so a task cannot change under us even though the sv-benchmarks repository moves on; the Zenodo DOI is what a paper cites.
